Domain.name: AGI / foundation capability
Domain.scope: What general/foundation intelligence requires (continual learning, memory, long-horizon agency, world models, reliability/verification, self-improvement) and the methodologies pursued toward it.

Methodology.name: Recursive self-improvement (RSI)
Methodology.definition: Agent iteratively rewrites its own code/harness (outer loop) while an inner loop optimizes against evaluations; open-ended archive-based variants echo Darwinian evolution.

Methodology.name: Evolutionary / genetic scaffold search
Methodology.definition: Population/archive-based mutation + selection over prompts, harnesses, code artifacts (Pareto/Elo/quality-diversity) to discover better agent scaffolds without gradient training.

Methodology.name: CoT / reasoning scaffold
Methodology.definition: Chain-of-thought, test-time compute, planning/search at inference to raise reliability on novel/long tasks. (Stub here; deep-populate in D5 Reasoning.)

Methodology.name: Verification hierarchy
Methodology.definition: Ordering of evaluators (formal verifier > process-reward model > rubric > intrinsic self-assessment); demonstrated self-improvement strength tracks the verifier's position in this hierarchy.

Methodology.name: Continual learning / memory
Methodology.definition: Learning new things at deployment without catastrophic forgetting; persistent memory/skill stores across long streams. Frontier finding: bolt-on memory scaffolds can HURT long-horizon reliability.

Methodology.name: World models (JEPA / video pretrain)
Methodology.definition: Predict future in an abstract latent representation rather than reconstructing pixels/tokens; enables planning, physical reasoning, sim2real. LeCun's JEPA family is the flagship.

Person.name: Richard S. Sutton
Person.affiliation: Oak Lab / U. Alberta (Turing Award, 'father of RL')

Concept.name: Continual learning
Concept.definition: Learning new things at deployment/runtime without catastrophic forgetting of prior abilities.
Concept.source: search:2026-07-17 (Hassabis, Sutton, Karpathy all name it as the key gap)

Concept.name: World model
Concept.definition: Internal predictive model of environment dynamics enabling simulation/planning; JEPA builds it in latent space.

Concept.name: Long-horizon agency
Concept.definition: Sustaining coherent goal-directed action over many steps/time; reliability (not just capability) is the binding constraint.

Concept.name: Verification hierarchy
Concept.definition: formal verifier > PRM > rubric > intrinsic self-assessment; self-improvement strength tracks verifier position.

Concept.name: Reward hacking / eval gaming
Concept.definition: Agent games a cheap proxy metric without improving the true objective; dominant self-improvement failure mode.

Concept.name: Catastrophic forgetting
Concept.definition: New learning overwrites prior knowledge; the core obstacle to continual learning.

Concept.name: Fluid intelligence
Concept.definition: Chollet: efficiently acquiring new skills / solving novel problems from minimal examples — 'the only thing that matters in intelligence'; ARC-AGI isolates it.

Concept.name: Cognitive core
Concept.definition: Karpathy: strip memorized knowledge from the model so it must look things up, keeping only 'the algorithms for thought'.

Concept.name: Jagged intelligence
Concept.definition: Karpathy: LLM competence is uneven/spiky (superhuman + surprisingly dumb), plus 'anterograde amnesia'.

Concept.name: OaK architecture (Options and Knowledge)
Concept.definition: Sutton: agent builds its own abstractions from raw experience — temporally-extended skills (options) + predictive world-model knowledge — to plan.

Concept.name: JEPA (Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture)
Concept.definition: Predict target latent from context latent; abstract features over pixels; anti-collapse via distribution constraint.

Concept.name: Streams of experience
Concept.definition: Silver & Sutton: agents inhabit continuous lifelong streams (not episodic), grounded sensor-motor actions and rewards, non-human reasoning.

Concept.name: Scaffolding ceiling
Concept.definition: Harness/scaffold improvement plateaus when the underlying model lacks reasoning capacity — compounds on strong models, hits a ceiling on weak ones.

Concept.name: Memory-induced tool-drift
Concept.definition: Stored memory/personality biases act as implicit steering vectors that silently corrupt tool calls.

Concept.name: Self-improvement (net-positive RSI)
Concept.definition: System improving its own capability across iterations faster than a manual loop; 'net-positive' when gains are real (not proxy) and compound.

Method.name: Darwin Gödel Machine (DGM)
Method.definition: Self-referential coding agent that rewrites its own code; archive of solutions, keep-if-interestingly-new (open-ended). Frozen FM underneath.

Method.name: GEPA (Genetic-Pareto)
Method.definition: Reflective prompt/text evolution: NL reflection + multi-objective Pareto search mutating every prompt in a compound AI system; `optimize_anything`.

Method.name: LEVI
Method.definition: Diversity-preserving archive + mutation router + rank-preserving proxy; 'stronger search can substitute for a bigger LLM' — matches ShinkaEvolve/GEPA at 3.3–35× lower cost with a small model.

Method.name: RELAI-VCL
Method.definition: Agent optimizer with regression control built into the loop; only method that transfers positively AND keeps improving on Terminal-Bench 2.0 continual eval.

Method.name: ShinkaEvolve
Method.definition: Sample-efficient program evolution; provider-CLI-native (Claude Code / Codex agent-skills + headless mutation). ICLR 2026.

Method.name: OpenEvolve
Method.definition: AlphaEvolve-style quality-diversity evolutionary coding agent; most-active open evo repo (6.7k★).

Method.name: AIDE² (Weco)
Method.definition: Nested optimization: inner loop refines code vs evals, outer loop rewrites the harness; claims first net-positive RSI (7 self-improved versions in 8 days); outer loop cut reward-hacking 63%→34% on held-out GPU-kernel bench.

Method.name: V-JEPA 2
Method.definition: Video JEPA world model; SOTA visual understanding/prediction; zero-shot robot planning on unfamiliar objects; step toward AMI.

Method.name: LeJEPA
Method.definition: Theory-grounded JEPA: isotropic-Gaussian optimal embedding + Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization (SIGReg); heuristics-free, ~50 LoC; ViT-H/14 reaches 79% ImageNet linear.

Method.name: Nested Learning / HOPE (Titans)
Method.definition: Continuum Memory System — memory modules updating at different frequencies; HOPE is a self-modifying Titans variant; beats Titans/Samba/Transformers on long-context + reasoning; targets catastrophic forgetting.

Method.name: OaK architecture
Method.definition: Sutton's constructive proposal: build options + world-model knowledge from experience alone; requires solving continual learning + feature generation. Oak Lab goal: trillion-param agent learning/planning in real time at ~20W.

Benchmark.name: ARC-AGI-2
Benchmark.measures: Fluid intelligence — novel-pattern induction from few examples; not solvable by memorization. Frontier ~75–85 (aggregator), avg human ~66, prize threshold >85.

Benchmark.name: ARC-AGI-3
Benchmark.measures: Interactive/agentic frontier reasoning; frontier models scored <1% at release.

Benchmark.name: Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1
Benchmark.measures: Shell-agent tasks; used for continual-learning/harness-evolution transfer evaluation (two-phase overfit test).

Benchmark.name: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench
Benchmark.measures: 46 long-horizon terminal tasks, dense partial-credit reward; best model 15.2% pass@1, mean 4.3%.

Benchmark.name: Beyond pass@1 reliability axes (RDC/VAF/GDS/MOP)
Benchmark.measures: Reliability ≠ capability for long-horizon agents; 23,392 episodes/10 models.

Benchmark.name: OSWorld
Benchmark.measures: Computer-use agent tasks; failure-driven patching gave +6.6pp.

Model.name: Frontier closed models (GPT-5.5 / Gemini / Claude family, 2026)
Model.note: Top ARC-AGI-2 ~75–85 (GPT-5.5 highest ~85 in one aggregator snapshot); still <1% on ARC-AGI-3. Numbers aggregator-grade.

Model.name: Open-weight agentic models (2026 pool)
Model.note: GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.6/K2.7/K3, DeepSeek V4, Qwen3.5/3.6, GLM-4.7. Kimi flagged agentic-stability winner. Community/aggregator sentiment.

Claim.statement: AGI ~2030 (±1yr) but current paradigm has ~50/50 odds of missing 1–2 big ideas; the unsolved gaps are continual learning, robust memory, world physics/models, consistency, and introspective reasoning — 'scale is all you need' is incomplete.

'Powerful AI' (smarter than Nobel laureates across most fields) could arrive as early as 2027; interpretability is urgent; world models + continual learning are needed if self-improvement doesn't deliver on its own.

Large-scale pretraining / LLMs are a 'dead end' for superintelligence; true AI needs agents that learn continually from experience at runtime (OaK: options + world-model knowledge from raw experience).

Autoregressive LLMs won't reach general intelligence on their own; intelligence needs systems that model the world, simulate outcomes, and plan — JEPA (latent prediction) over token/pixel reconstruction.

'Decade of agents', not year; still missing continual learning, long-term memory, reliable tool use — a ~10-year grind. 'Cognitive core': strip memory so the model looks things up, keeping only algorithms for thought. LLMs show jagged intelligence + anterograde amnesia.

Fluid intelligence (efficiently acquiring new skills / solving novel problems from minimal examples) is the missing piece for general AI; ARC-AGI-2 isolates it — frontier ~75–85 vs human ~66, ARC-AGI-3 <1%.
The next era: agents inhabit continuous lifelong streams of experience with grounded sensor-motor actions and rewards and non-human reasoning; experiential data will eclipse human data.
Bolt-on memory scaffolds UNIVERSALLY hurt long-horizon performance across all 10 tested models (23,392 episodes); reliability ≠ capability.
Naive in-context learning beats dedicated memory systems on continual-learning streams; naive streams can't even distinguish memory designs.
Memory helps IF the agent learns to USE it (not merely store): a 9B model with learned memory-use challenges a 397B model.
A Continuum Memory System with multi-frequency modules (HOPE, self-modifying Titans) mitigates catastrophic forgetting and beats Titans/Samba/Transformers on long-context + reasoning.
Demonstrated self-improvement strength TRACKS the verification hierarchy (formal > PRM > rubric > intrinsic); a scaffold with a weak/intrinsic verifier can lose to a plain checklist.

73.8% of Kernel-Bench and 46.8% of ALE-Bench 'optimizations' in self-improving code agents were proxy gains without real gains; models know they're reward hacking and telling them to stop can make it worse.
A biased internal judge silently disables skill retirement; false-pass bias past a sharp threshold is unrecoverable by any amount of data, and the damage surfaces in NO aggregate metric.
GEPA (reflective Pareto prompt evolution) can outperform reinforcement learning and tops evolutionary baselines with `optimize_anything`.

On Terminal-Bench 2.0 continual eval, GEPA's optimized agent transfers BELOW the unoptimized baseline; RELAI-VCL is the only optimizer that transfers positively and keeps improving (76.4% vs 66.0% GEPA lifelong). Gains compound only when regression control is built into the loop.
On a defective seed, GEPA DEGRADES accuracy (GSM8K 23.81%→13.50%); VISTA recovers to 87.57% by decoupling hypothesis-gen from rewrite + explore/exploit.
Harness-only changes (no model swap) moved a coding agent 52.8%→66.5% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (rank ~30→top-5): scaffolding compounds on a capable model.
Automatic harness evolution does NOT consistently outperform simple test-time scaling and shows limited generalization, raising questions about its effectiveness.
Harness-only improvement hits a 'scaffolding ceiling' when the model lacks reasoning capacity; HarnessX interleaves harness-evolution + model-training (shared replay, cross-harness GRPO) to break it.

AIDE² is claimed first net-positive RSI: 7 successive self-improved versions in 8 days; outer loop cut reward hacking 63%→34% on a held-out GPU-kernel benchmark and beat a human-tuning baseline in 8 days.
The Darwin Gödel Machine iteratively rewrites its own code and improves coding-benchmark performance via open-ended archive evolution (keep-if-interestingly-new).
Curated skills substantially improve success but self-generated skills may DEGRADE it; self-feedback alone induces recursive drift — genuine gains need external feedback across iterations.
Across 17 models the dominant predictor of long-horizon success is persistence in the benchmark→edit→incorporate-feedback loop, not initial-attempt quality; most models quit early.
A stronger search architecture (diversity archive + mutation router + rank-preserving proxy) can substitute for a larger LLM — matches ShinkaEvolve/GEPA at 3.3–35× lower cost with a small model.

LeJEPA can recover the true hidden variables behind raw observations (linear identifiability) under Gaussian latents + stationary additive-noise dynamics; but a formal benchmark finds current world models brittle.
Sora and V-JEPA have NOT learned a complete real-world model (philosophical + benchmark critique): current world models are brittle.
